case_name: KAREN HILL v TAMAKI LABOUR HIRE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [72] The restructuring process and decision to dismiss Ms Hill was not what a fair and reasonable employer could have done in all the circumstances at the time. Ms Hill has established she had a personal grievance for unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of redundancy rationale, process, suspension, remedies and s 124. The Authority found both the dismissal and suspension unjustified.
remedies_awarded: One week's lost wages; $23,000 compensation ($18,000 dismissal and $5,000 suspension).

case_name: HARRISON RICHARDS v LAWNS TREES AND GARDENS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [47] I find that the dismissal was both procedurally and substantively unjustified.
review_notes: Direct review of abandonment issue, dismissal justification, remedies and contribution. The Authority found no abandonment and an unjustified dismissal.
remedies_awarded: $9,600 compensation after 20% contribution reduction; $1,000 records penalty payable to the Authority.

case_name: STEVE NOTMAN v TRANSPOWER NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [1] Mr Notman remains employed by Transpower; his claims are unjustified-disadvantage claims associated with the COVID-19 vaccination policy.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this determination does not decide a dismissal or constructive-dismissal grievance. It concerns unjustified disadvantage only, so it is outside the dismissal-merits denominator.
remedies_awarded: $5,000 compensation for an established unjustified disadvantage; no dismissal remedy.

case_name: ANDRIES GOUWS v OPTIMAL FIRE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [22] For the reasons given, and on the Authority’s own motion, these three matters are to be removed to the Employment Court to hear and determine.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a removal determination under s 178. The Authority did not determine the merits of the Gouws dismissal grievances.
remedies_awarded: No merits remedies; matters removed to the Employment Court.

case_name: MARK BROWN v TPS NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [166] Mr Brown had not established personal grievances of unjustified dismissal or grievances of unjustified disadvantage arising from the restructuring proposal and how it was decided and carried out. His personal grievance application to the Authority is declined.
review_notes: Direct review of restructuring rationale, consultation, redeployment and summary. TPS established genuine business reasons and acted reasonably and fairly in the restructuring and redeployment process.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; personal grievance declined.

case_name: MONISHA LATA and JADE MOOLMAN v EMPLOYMENT GROUP LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [38] I am satisfied Ms Lata was constructively dismissed by EGL. [52] Accordingly, Ms Moolman established her claim for unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of both applicants' dismissal claims. Ms Lata's resignation was a constructive dismissal caused by EGL's unreasonable conduct; Ms Moolman's trial-period dismissal was unjustified.
remedies_awarded: Ms Lata: $15,000 lost wages + $20,000 compensation. Ms Moolman: $30,000 lost wages + $20,000 compensation. Shared $4,500 costs plus filing fees.

case_name: BRANDON BARRETT v BPD CONSTRUCTION LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [38] BPD has not discharged the onus of establishing its actions were justified in accordance with s 103A of the Act and as a result Mr Barrett’s dismissal was unjustified.
review_notes: Direct review of whether Mr Barrett resigned or was dismissed, justification, remedies, contribution and counterclaim. The Authority found dismissal by BPD and no fair process or good reason.
remedies_awarded: $13,572 lost wages; $12,000 compensation; counterclaim declined.

case_name: SHIBO CHEN v CONSTRUST LIMITED and YUHANG (DEREK) DAI
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Mr Dai’s actions, and how he acted, was not what a fair and reasonable employer could have done in all the circumstances. He was therefore unable to justify Mr Chen’s dismissal. Accordingly, Mr Chen’s unjustified dismissal personal grievance claim succeeded.
review_notes: Direct review of employee status, dismissal/constructive dismissal, justification, remedies and contribution. Mr Chen was a permanent employee and was dismissed when work was withheld; alternatively the breaches also amounted to constructive dismissal.
remedies_awarded: $5,236.53 lost remuneration; $20,000 compensation; wage/holiday arrears, petrol allowance, interest and partial penalty also ordered.

case_name: WENDY DAWN VITA v THE CAMPION COLLEGE BOARD
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [65] Ms Wendy Dawn Vita has a personal grievance in that she was unjustifiably disadvantaged in her employment.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this determination concerns unjustified disadvantage and good-faith failures only. It does not determine a dismissal or constructive-dismissal grievance and is outside the dismissal-merits denominator.
remedies_awarded: $15,000 compensation for unjustified disadvantage; no dismissal remedy.

case_name: JOSH RARAVULA v NORTHERN RESCUE HELICOPTER LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [103] NRHL adopted a process with unjustifiable elements and breached its duty of good faith to Mr Raravula and he was disadvantaged by that.
review_notes: Direct review confirms Mr Raravula remained employed and challenged a roster change. This determination decides unjustified disadvantage/discrimination, not dismissal merits.
remedies_awarded: $10,000 compensation for unjustified disadvantage; no dismissal remedy.

case_name: XINHUA HAO v SOUTH POLE IP HOLDING (NZ) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [66] Mr Hao succeeded in his personal grievance application because his resignation on 26 January 2023 was really a constructive dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of constructive-dismissal findings, contribution, arrears and orders. South Pole's employment breaches caused the resignation and no contributory reduction was required.
remedies_awarded: $15,000 compensation; $4,920 wages; $8,200 annual-leave arrears; filing fee reimbursement.

case_name: SHAUNA DWYER v OAKVUE BLOODSTOCK LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [77] I do not accept Ms Dwyer’s resignation amounted to a constructive dismissal. Accordingly, Ms Dwyer’s claim of unjustified dismissal does not succeed.
review_notes: Direct review of the constructive-dismissal claim and the separate successful unjustified-disadvantage claim. The dismissal merits claim failed even though bullying-related disadvantage succeeded.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $10,000 compensation was awarded for the separate unjustified-disadvantage grievance.

case_name: PRAKASH MISTRY v GOODMAN FIELDER LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [64] The Authority grants leave to raise the personal grievance in relation to Mr Mistry’s dismissal. In accordance with s 114(5) of the Act, there will now be a direction to the parties to attend further mediation.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a preliminary time-limit determination granting leave to raise the dismissal grievance out of time. It does not determine dismissal merits.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal-merits remedies; leave granted and matter directed to further mediation.

case_name: TINA HOUKAMAU v WASTE MANAGEMENT LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [44] I am satisfied that WML was justified in summarily dismissing Ms Houkamau for serious misconduct. [70] As Ms Houkamau’s claim for unjustified dismissal has not been made out, there are no orders made with respect to her claim.
review_notes: Direct merits review and second review of the serious-misconduct findings. The Authority accepted WML's evidential basis, found serious misconduct, loss of trust and confidence, and a procedurally fair summary dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy. Ms Houkamau was ordered to pay $4,000 penalty to WML and $2,000 to the Crown for separate IEA/good-faith breaches.

case_name: TIMOTHY RYDER v LEOPARD LINE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [22] For the above reasons, I find Mr Ryder was unjustifiably dismissed by LLL on 2 November 2022, with his dismissal confirmed by Mr Eade’s email of 3 November 2022.
review_notes: Direct review of this second determination, which decides dismissal justification after the earlier preliminary employment-status determination. LLL failed to raise concerns adequately or give Mr Ryder a reasonable opportunity to respond; the defects were not minor.
remedies_awarded: Order records $20,900 compensation and $3,920 lost wages; no contribution reduction.

case_name: AARON YAQUB v NEILSONS LAWYERS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [1] The Authority issued a determination on 6 March 2025 which found Mr Yaqub had established personal grievances for unjustified disadvantage and unjustified dismissal for which he was awarded remedies. Costs were reserved.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is the later costs determination only. The underlying merits determination is 2025 NZERA 139; counting this costs follow-up would duplicate the merits case.
remedies_awarded: Costs only: NLL ordered to pay Mr Yaqub $22,000 plus filing fee and MYL $3,500.

case_name: FTT v SINCLAIR PRYOR MOTORS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [77](b) FTT has not established their resignation was an unjustified constructive dismissal, as I do not consider it was reasonably foreseeable FTT would resign in the circumstances.
review_notes: Direct review of the constructive-dismissal claim separately from the successful sexual-harassment investigation/disadvantage grievance. The dismissal merits claim failed.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy. Separate unjustified-disadvantage remedies included lost wages for the relevant period and $15,000 compensation.

case_name: LEE POWNALL v NATIONAL ADVOCACY TRUST
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [18] Except for NAT’s failure to provide Mr Pownall the CoS within seven days of the RoS being signed, the issues raised by Mr Pownall are not relevant. [35] The National Advocacy Trust is to pay, within 28 days of this determination, $500.00 into the Crown’s bank account.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is enforcement of a certified Record of Settlement/certificate-of-service breach. The Authority rejected attempts to re-litigate the original employment dispute; it does not determine dismissal merits.
remedies_awarded: $500 penalty to the Crown for the settlement breach; no dismissal-merits remedy.

case_name: KALANI HENDERSON v NC HOSPITALITY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [43] Ms Kalani Henderson has a personal grievance in that she was unjustifiably (constructively) dismissed.
review_notes: Direct review of the constructive-dismissal analysis, remedies and contribution. The unilateral reduction in hours/duties caused the resignation; Ms Henderson did not contribute to the circumstances.
remedies_awarded: $1,362 gross lost remuneration and $15,000 compensation; no contribution reduction.

case_name: ALISTAIR HUTT v FIRE AND EMERGENCY NEW ZEALAND
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [1] Mr Hutt worked for FENZ until he retired on 1 May 2024. He says FENZ should have paid him a retirement gratuity. [74] Mr Hutt does not succeed in his unjust enrichment claim.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a retirement-gratuity dispute/unjustified-disadvantage and unjust-enrichment matter. Mr Hutt retired; no dismissal or constructive-dismissal merits are determined.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; retirement gratuity/unjust-enrichment claims failed.

case_name: HD CONTRACTOR LIMITED v ZE HOU
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [1] This is an application by HD Contractor Limited for compliance of a costs order made against Ze Hou when he was unsuccessful in the Authority with his claims of unjustified disadvantage, unjustified dismissal and alleged wage arrears.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a compliance proceeding for an earlier costs order, not a merits determination. The underlying dismissal merits were decided in 2024 NZERA 409.
remedies_awarded: Compliance/costs only: $8,663.56 costs payable by $100 weekly instalments plus filing fee.

case_name: CAMERON RIX v ROTORUA QUARRY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: In my determination of 13 March 2025, I upheld Mr Rix’s claims of unjustified dismissal and awarded remedies. I left the question of costs to be quantified and/or resolved by the parties.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a consent costs determination only. The underlying merits decision is 2025 NZERA 152 and must carry the legal classification without duplicating this follow-up.
remedies_awarded: Costs only: Rotorua Quarry Limited ordered by consent to pay Mr Rix $5,500.

case_name: DAYNAH OLLIVER and SHEENA TAYLOR v TE ARAROA & DISTRICT PROGRESSIVE ASSOCIATION INCORPORATED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [30] TADPAI has not been able to justify dismissing the applicants and it follows I find their personal grievance claims for unjustified dismissal are successful.
review_notes: Direct review of fixed-term status, dismissal, disadvantage, remedies and contribution. TADPAI could not rely on fixed-term expiry and followed no fair dismissal process; neither applicant contributed to the grievances.
remedies_awarded: Olliver: $37,500 compensation plus 13 weeks lost wages and arrears. Taylor: $27,500 compensation plus 13 weeks lost wages and holiday arrears.

case_name: HENRY PENNY v FRELLO LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [47] I find the dismissal to be both substantively and procedurally unjustified and Henry Penny is entitled to an assessment of remedies.
review_notes: Direct review of redundancy rationale/selection, remedies and contribution. The selection criteria/matrix process was not sufficiently fair or transparent; redundancy was both substantively and procedurally unjustified.
remedies_awarded: $20,000 compensation plus three weeks lost wages; no contribution reduction.

case_name: MARKUS PAETZ v SOLLY’S FREIGHT (1978) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [74] Neither of Solly’s breaches are such to support a finding of constructive dismissal – I am not satisfied that in the circumstances it was foreseeable that Mr Paetz would resign in response to the breaches nor am I satisfied that he did resign because of the two breaches alone.
review_notes: Direct review resolves the apparent typo in paragraph [98]: the operative constructive-dismissal analysis at [73]-[76] expressly rejects dismissal and upholds only two unjustified-disadvantage grievances.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $14,000 compensation for separate unjustified-disadvantage grievances.

case_name: CARA PARKINS v FLIGHT CENTRE (NZ) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [52] Flight Centre’s decision to disestablish Ms Parkins’ role and the way it went about doing so were consistent with what a fair and reasonable employer could have done in the circumstances. Accordingly, Ms Parkins has not succeeded in establishing her personal grievance.
review_notes: Direct review of genuine commercial reasons, consultation and redeployment. Flight Centre justified both the redundancy decision and process.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; personal grievance unsuccessful.

case_name: JOSHUA GRAHAM v PRECISION LAWN MOWING LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [8] In Mr Graham’s absence he has been unable to establish a case to answer. I have therefore decided to dismiss the matter in accordance with s 173 of the Employment Relations Act 2000. [9] Mr Graham’s claims are dismissed.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a non-prosecution/procedural dismissal of the Authority proceeding after the applicant failed to attend. The Authority did not decide the redundancy merits.
remedies_awarded: No merits remedies; proceeding dismissed under s 173.

case_name: NATHAN PETRIE v ALPHERO LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [80] As I have found there has not been a breach of duty by Alphero, Mr Petrie’s claim for unjustifiable (constructive) dismissal must also fail. [84] No orders are made.
review_notes: Direct review of the remote-work arrangement, unjustified-disadvantage and constructive-dismissal claims. The 4:1 arrangement was temporary and Alphero committed no repudiatory breach.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; claims failed.

case_name: ANTONIOS ZIOGAS v THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [601]-[606] It has not been established the rotation decision was predetermined or that the Department failed to consult with Mr Ziogas ... Mr Ziogas was not constructively dismissed.
review_notes: Direct review of causation, consultation and constructive dismissal. The Department's later review/record/leave failures supported separate disadvantage grievances, but did not cause the resignation or make it a dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $12,500 compensation for separate unjustified-disadvantage grievances.

case_name: JAN FRANCES LOVE and JUDITH CRESTANI v WHARE MANAAKI INCORPORATED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Conclusion: The application for interim reinstatement is unsuccessful. Costs are reserved and will be dealt with after the substantive determination in respect of this matter has issued.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this determination decides only interim reinstatement. It expressly leaves the substantive unjustified-dismissal merits for a later determination.
remedies_awarded: No merits remedy; interim reinstatement declined.

case_name: JANET DU FALL v THE MOKOIA INTERMEDIATE SCHOOL BOARD
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [1] Mrs Du Fall raised a range of claims, initially related to pay and performance reviews and whether she was paid correctly. [136] The orders concern compensation for pay-review/performance-appraisal disadvantage and wage/holiday arrears.
review_notes: Direct review of the stated issues and orders confirms there is no dismissal or constructive-dismissal grievance in this determination; it concerns pay, performance reviews, arrears and disadvantage.
remedies_awarded: $2,500 compensation for disadvantage plus overtime, annual-leave work, public-holiday arrears and alternative holidays.

case_name: SCOTT MARTINSEN v LONE PINE TROPHY STUD LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [8] The issues requiring investigation and determination were unjustified disadvantage, wage arrears, public-holiday pay, work-vehicle damages and costs; no dismissal grievance is listed.
review_notes: Direct review confirms Mr Martinsen left employment but did not plead or obtain a dismissal/constructive-dismissal merits determination. This is a disadvantage and wage-arrears case.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $13,600 compensation after 20% contribution plus $39,832.30 wage arrears and public-holiday amounts.

case_name: BALJINDER SINGH v PILLING & LEGGETT ENGINEERING CO LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [43] I find that the dismissal was both procedurally and substantively unjustified.
review_notes: Direct review of the purported trial-period dismissal, performance concerns, remedies and contribution. The employer had neither a proper process nor a substantiated reason for dismissal.
remedies_awarded: $15,000 compensation and $1,760 lost wages; separate $800 records penalty.

case_name: JOSHUA KNOX v RECRUIT IT GROUP LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [38] Having reviewed the evidence, I find that Mr Knox’s dismissal by redundancy was not only substantively unjustified, but also procedurally unjustified. [66] Mr Knox’s claim ... has been made out.
review_notes: Direct review of the redundancy business case, consultation, remedies and contribution. The information and rationale were materially inconsistent and consultation was not genuine.
remedies_awarded: $2,884.62 lost wages and $18,000 compensation.

case_name: CRAIG PAULSEN v THE ELECTORAL COMMISSION
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Employment Relationship Problem: Mr Paulsen raised four disadvantage grievance claims concerning a suspension and how the Commission investigated and addressed employment concerns ... including a written warning for serious misconduct.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this determination concerns unjustified disadvantage during continuing employment, not dismissal. Three disadvantage grievances succeeded.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $16,000 compensation after 20% contribution for disadvantage.

case_name: JOSEPH PARR v IN YOUR POCKET MEDIA LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [51] Accordingly I find that Mr Parr’s claim for unjustified (constructive) dismissal is made out on these grounds.
review_notes: Direct review of employer breaches, causation, remedies and contribution. The breaches were repudiatory and caused Mr Parr's resignation; the alternative disadvantage claim was not separately remedied.
remedies_awarded: $8,294.87 lost wages and $20,000 compensation; no contribution reduction.

case_name: CHONGXUAN ZHANG v MAYS PROPERTY DEVELOPMENT LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [48] The threshold for constructive dismissal is high, and I find is not met in this case. [49] I determine that Mr Zhang was not constructively dismissed by MPDL.
review_notes: Direct review of the resignation, alleged bullying/abusive call and constructive-dismissal test. Separate employer conduct amounted to unjustified disadvantage, but the resignation was not a dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $9,000 compensation after 10% contribution for separate unjustified disadvantage.

case_name: ELLIOTT ROE v AIRBUS NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [95] For the reasons given Mr Roe had not established grounds for a personal grievance of unjustified dismissal. [96] Airbus's actions ... were what a fair and reasonable employer could have done in all the circumstances at the time.
review_notes: Direct review of the COVID-19 vaccination worksite requirement, consultation, alternatives and process. Airbus reasonably explored alternatives and justified termination; the identified process defect caused no unfairness.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; personal grievance declined.

case_name: HAI ZHENG v JCD NZ LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [79] Ultimately the employment relationship ended at his volition. He did not have a personal grievance of unjustified dismissal. [96] His purported resignation did not amount to a constructive dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of the actual/constructive-dismissal claim separately from successful disadvantage claims. JCD had committed prior breaches, but had taken steps to address concerns and the later resignation was not reasonably foreseeable.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $10,000 compensation for separate disadvantage plus part of a $5,000 penalty.

case_name: ASMITA ELLIOT v HE HERENGA KURA TRUST
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [593]-[599] I conclude Ms Elliot felt she had no choice but to resign and this should have been reasonably foreseeable to HHKT ... Ms Elliot was unjustifiably constructively dismissed.
review_notes: Direct review of workplace-safety/good-faith breaches, causation, remedies and contribution. The unsafe home meeting and subsequent conduct caused a breakdown of trust and the resignation; no contribution reduction was warranted.
remedies_awarded: $25,000 compensation and $6,982.49 gross lost wages; no contribution reduction.

case_name: ABC First Applicant DEF Second Applicant GHI Third Applicant JKL Fourth v MNO
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [53] If, following mediation, the applicants wish the investigation of this employment relationship problem to continue, they should advise the Authority. A case management conference will then be convened to timetable an investigation meeting of the substantive employment relationship problem.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is an interim reinstatement-to-payroll determination concerning unpaid suspension. The Authority found only an arguable case and expressly left the substantive employment relationship problem for later investigation.
remedies_awarded: Interim payroll reinstatement granted; substantive merits not determined.

case_name: JEROME LAZARO v WAIMEA CONTRACT CARRIERS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [82] WCC did not dismiss Mr Lazaro. As a result, Mr Lazaro cannot establish a personal grievance for unjustified dismissal. [88] WCC did not unjustifiably dismiss Mr Lazaro.
review_notes: Direct review of the alleged dismissal and alternative unsafe-workplace grievance. The 4 December meeting was not an unequivocal sending away and could not reasonably be interpreted as dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; employment relationship problem resolved in favour of WCC.

case_name: YPC v D & L DECORATORS (2021) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Orders: I am not satisfied that YPC’s delay in raising a personal grievance was occasioned by exceptional circumstances and consequently I decline to grant leave to YPC to raise a personal grievance out of time.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a preliminary leave/out-of-time determination. It does not decide whether the redundancy dismissal was justified.
remedies_awarded: Leave to raise the dismissal grievance out of time declined; no dismissal merits determination.

case_name: HELEN KOSTER v THE CHIEF OF NEW ZEALAND DEFENCE FORCE
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [173] For the reasons above Ms Koster has not established the grounds for her disadvantage personal grievance claims and her personal grievance claims have been unsuccessful.
review_notes: Direct review confirms the pleaded claims concern COVID-19 related unjustified disadvantage, not dismissal or constructive dismissal. The Authority rejected those disadvantage claims.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; disadvantage claims unsuccessful.

case_name: MARLIES HIEMER v STYLE CLUB NZ LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [38] Ms Hiemer has not been successful because she was not an employee and will not be entitled to pursue a personal grievance claim.
review_notes: Direct review confirms the offer was withdrawn before an employment relationship was formed. There is therefore no dismissal-merits claim within the employee dismissal denominator.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; applicant was not an employee.

case_name: THOMAS CULLY v THE WORK SHOP LIMITED (IN LIQUIDATION)
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [52] Accordingly I find that his claim for unjustified (constructive) dismissal is made out on these grounds. [61] Mr Cully’s claim ... has been made out.
review_notes: Direct review of the employer's wage-payment breaches, refusal to mediate and causation. Those breaches made continued employment untenable and caused Mr Cully's resignation.
remedies_awarded: $3,201.49 lost wages and $12,000 compensation; no contribution reduction.

case_name: BRETT SIMMONS v RAINBOW CONFECTIONERY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [60] When Mr Simmons’ dismissal on the grounds of redundancy and the actions that RCL took at the time are seen through the lens of the test of justification at s 103A of the Act, I find the dismissal to be what a fair and reasonable employer could have done in all the circumstances at the time.
review_notes: Direct review of the genuine commercial rationale, consultation, selection and post-restructure duties. The Authority accepted the redundancy as justified.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: BRIAN GREEN v PROPERTY SERVICES UNLIMITED (WAIKATO) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [45] I order Mr Green to pay $2,533.92 to Property Services Unlimited (Waikato) Limited as a contribution to 60 percent of their legal costs.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a costs determination after Mr Green stopped engaging with the Authority. It does not determine dismissal merits.
remedies_awarded: Costs only: $2,533.92 contribution ordered against Mr Green.

case_name: DINO GOVERNOR v DANIEL RIDDIFORD
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [11] The issues requiring investigation and determination are wage arrears, breach of employment agreement, statutory/good-faith obligations, penalties, interest and costs.
review_notes: Direct review confirms that although the employment ended in contested circumstances, this determination does not include a dismissal or constructive-dismissal grievance among the issues it decides.
remedies_awarded: $4,398.34 gross arrears plus interest; one ACC-related arrears issue deferred.

case_name: ANGHARAD O’BRIEN v THE PLATFORM MEDIA NZ LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [5] This determination does not deal with the dismissal related claims which were ultimately the subject of a separate investigation and in relation to which a separate determination will issue.
review_notes: Direct review resolves misleading later wording in the order. This determination decides pre-dismissal unjustified-disadvantage claims only and expressly excludes the dismissal claims for a separate determination.
remedies_awarded: $17,550 compensation after 10% contribution for the disadvantage grievances; dismissal merits reserved for a separate determination.

case_name: JUDITH BELL v HUBERGROUP NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [84] I find the decision to disestablish Ms Bell’s role substantively unjustified. [101] Hubergroup’s decision to disestablish Ms Bell’s role was procedurally unjustified. [102] Ms Bell is successful in her claim of unjustifiable dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of the redundancy rationale, information/consultation process, remedies and contribution. The redundancy lacked sufficient evidence of superfluousness and the process had substantial fairness defects.
remedies_awarded: $18,333.68 lost wages and $25,000 compensation; no contribution reduction.

case_name: HAILONG ZHU v GREEN HOLDING CONSTRUCTION LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [3] This new information has had the effect of confining this investigation into one issue only namely whether there has been a breach of the RoS. [13] Mr Zhu has no arguable case against the respondents who have not breached the agreed terms of settlement with him.
review_notes: Direct review confirms the underlying redundancy/dismissal dispute had been resolved by a binding written Record of Settlement. This determination only addresses compliance with that settlement and does not decide dismissal merits.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal-merits remedy; no breach of the settlement found.

case_name: MICHAEL SOMERVILLE v VORTEX DISTRIBUTORS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [111] Mr Somerville’s dismissal was unjustified due to procedural defects in the process which were not minor and resulted in him being treated unfairly. [120] His dismissal was unjustified on procedural grounds.
review_notes: Direct review and second review of the legal/monetary disagreement. Vortex had substantive justification for two allegations, but serious procedural unfairness made the dismissal legally unjustified. Mr Somerville's substantial culpability warranted a 75% remedies reduction.
remedies_awarded: $3,750 dismissal compensation after contribution plus lost wages to 4 October 2023 less 75%; separate $5,000 disadvantage compensation.

case_name: PAUL SO’O’ULA v WESLEY COLLEGE TRUST BOARD
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [90] The Authority accepts that the Trust Board was justified taking the action to dismiss Mr So’o’ula. It was a decision that a fair and reasonable employer could have made in all the circumstances ... Mr So’o’ula’s grievance claim for unjustified dismissal is unsuccessful. [93] The dismissal ... was both substantively and procedurally justified.
review_notes: Direct review of the disciplinary findings, disparity argument and process. The Trust Board reasonably differentiated between employees based on responsibility, conduct and responses, and justified dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; reinstatement and other remedies declined.

case_name: PREETI MALA v SPECTRUM CARE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [3] This determination deals only with the preliminary jurisdictional issue of whether Ms Mala has raised all the personal grievances she seeks to bring before the Authority within the statutory 90-day timeframe. [19] The unjustified constructive dismissal claim remains before the Authority to investigate and determine.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a preliminary jurisdiction/time-limit determination. It identifies the constructive-dismissal grievance for later merits investigation but does not decide it.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal merits remedy; substantive grievances left for later investigation.

case_name: IAN KEVIN RENNER v MANAWATU MOTORS 1970 LIMITED (t/a ROBERTSON MOTORS)
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Employment Relationship Problem: Mr Renner's employment ended with his resignation effective 8 September 2023. His claims concern unjustified suspension, annual-leave deductions, unpaid commissions and related obligations.
review_notes: Direct review confirms there is no dismissal or constructive-dismissal claim. The determination addresses suspension/disadvantage, commissions, good faith, confidentiality and restraint issues after a resignation.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; commission entitlement to be quantified, no penalty ordered.

case_name: ICARO ANDRE RIBEIRO v HEB CONSTRUCTION LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [28] I find that in all the circumstances, Mr Ribeiro was not dismissed but resigned. [32] There is no evidence to suggest that Mr Ribeiro’s resignation was driven by HEB, or that HEB breached its obligations towards Mr Ribeiro. Accordingly, I find that Mr Ribeiro has no personal grievance claim for unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of whether employment ended by dismissal or resignation and the alternative constructive-dismissal theory. The Authority found a voluntary resignation and no employer breach causing it.
remedies_awarded: No orders; dismissal and disadvantage claims failed.

case_name: JOSHUA MCCLUNG v WAINUI HIGHLANDS TRUST
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [42] I have found in favour of WHT in that Mr McClung resigned and accordingly his unjustified dismissal grievance claim is unsuccessful. [73] Mr McClung has been unsuccessful with all his claims against Wainui Highlands Trust.
review_notes: Direct review of how the short fixed-term employment ended, alleged bullying and information-request disadvantage. The Authority preferred evidence that Mr McClung resigned and rejected all claims.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; all claims unsuccessful.

case_name: JUNIOR TAUFUA v THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [72] Mr Taufua’s actions were sufficient to amount to serious misconduct, and were sufficiently serious to justify dismissal ... The decision to dismiss was within the range of options available to the Department acting as a fair and reasonable employer. [73] Mr Taufua’s personal grievance claim of unjustified dismissal ... is not made out.
review_notes: Direct second review of serious misconduct, investigation and decision-making. Corrections adequately investigated, involved Mr Taufua and genuinely considered his position before a justified dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No orders; dismissal/disadvantage/good-faith claims not made out.

case_name: DAVID BAHLER v TRANSPORTATION AUCKLAND CORPORATION LIMITED (trading as NZ BUS)
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [53] The decision to dismiss Mr Bahler was substantively justified. [59] The process NZ Bus followed ... considered [his comments] before it made its decision to end the employment relationship for serious misconduct. The application is unsuccessful and is declined.
review_notes: Direct second review of the serious-misconduct finding, driving history, alternatives and process. The Authority found the latest incident and pattern of unsafe driving destroyed trust and confidence and justified dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; application declined.

case_name: NICKA PAPERA v THE RECRUITMENT NETWORK LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Outcome: Mr Papera has not been successful. His grievance claims were not lodged in the Authority within the statutory time frames and the Authority has no jurisdiction to proceed with those claims.
review_notes: Direct review confirms the Authority disposed of the personal-grievance claims on statutory time/jurisdiction grounds and did not determine dismissal justification. The wage claims were separately rejected on payment evidence.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal-merits remedy; grievance claims barred by statutory time limits.

case_name: NICKOLA MAKING v ALAN WINDLE
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Conclusion: ... there is no new information relied on that was not available at the time the Authority determined the matter ... the application for reopening is declined.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a reopening/follow-up determination. The underlying 5 March 2025 determination had already rejected Ms Making's medical-incapacity dismissal grievance; this decision only refuses to reopen it and must not duplicate the merits case.
remedies_awarded: No new dismissal-merits remedy; reopening application declined.

case_name: JLG v DAX
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The basis for there being a dismissal at the initiative of DAX has not been made out ... JLG has not established that there was an unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of how the employment ended. The evidence did not establish an employer-initiated dismissal; separate annual-leave entitlement succeeded.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; 10 weeks annual leave ordered, other claims unsuccessful.

case_name: AMANDA VAN ZYL v ANGLO ENGINEERING LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [42] Her actions in forging a document namely a COVID test module, qualifies as serious misconduct. [56] Both the decision to dismiss Ms van Zyl, and the requirements of procedural fairness ... were met by Anglo. The personal grievance application is unsuccessful and is declined.
review_notes: Direct second review of serious misconduct, alternatives and dismissal process. The Authority found deliberate forgery, resulting loss of trust/confidence and a substantively and procedurally justified dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; personal grievance declined.

case_name: ANDREW BYRNE v RUSHMORE DISTRIBUTORS (NZ) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [36] In summary, Mr Byrne’s dismissal for redundancy on 14 February 2025 was unjustified ... information relevant to the restructuring proposal and selection criteria was not fairly shared, and RDL breached the requirement to consult about redeployment options.
review_notes: Direct review of redundancy genuineness, selection/process, redeployment, remedies and contribution. The dismissal failed because consultation and redeployment obligations were materially breached.
remedies_awarded: Three months ordinary remuneration plus holiday pay/KiwiSaver; $16,000 compensation; vehicle/fuel benefit for three months; no contribution reduction.

case_name: SIDDANTH PRASAD and NISHAL NIKESH LAL and AMIT VERMA and MUKESHWAR PRASAD v FIJI FOOD DISTRIBUTORS NZ LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [61] FFDL unjustifiably dismissed each applicant.
review_notes: Direct review of the four applicants' dismissal, disadvantage and wage claims. The Authority expressly found each applicant was unjustifiably dismissed and ordered remedies for all four.
remedies_awarded: $32,000 compensation to each applicant plus substantial individual wage arrears; Mr Verma also awarded $8,000 for an unlawful premium.

case_name: NATASHIA CORBY v VIRTUAL PLUMBING LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Conclusion: The delay in raising the grievance was occasioned by exceptional circumstances and leave is granted for Ms Corby to raise her personal grievance claim outside the expiration of the employee notification period. Before any further steps ... the parties are directed to attend mediation.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a preliminary leave/out-of-time determination. It permits the termination grievance to proceed but does not decide dismissal justification.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal-merits remedy; leave granted and mediation directed.

case_name: SAJ v IGD
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [9] The issue for determination is whether an interim order should be made regarding the disciplinary action by IGD against SAJ. [24] I order that IGD is to take no further steps in its disciplinary process regarding SAJ until 9am on Monday 10 November 2025.
review_notes: Direct review confirms an interim disciplinary-process injunction only. SAJ remained employed and no dismissal merits had yet arisen; substantive issues were awaiting determination.
remedies_awarded: Temporary restraint on disciplinary process only; no dismissal-merits remedy.

case_name: THE ESTATE OF ANTHONY DALE KAHAKI v COMMISSIONER OF POLICE
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [93] SC Kahaki was unjustifiably disadvantaged in his employment ... [100] The Commissioner of Police is to pay the estate ... compensation of $25,000.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this determination concerns unjustified disadvantage during continuing employment and disciplinary warning/process issues. It does not determine a dismissal or constructive-dismissal grievance.
remedies_awarded: $25,000 compensation plus filing-fee reimbursement for disadvantage; no dismissal remedy.

case_name: CAMERON WONG v OBERS BROTHERS CONSTRUCTION LIMITED in liquidation
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: As Obers was not there to justify or speak to its actions, it follows that I find Mr Wong’s dismissal unjustified. Summary of orders: Obers Brothers Construction Limited has unjustifiably dismissed Cameron Wong.
review_notes: Direct review of the dismissal evidence and remedies. The employer did not participate or justify its conduct, so the Authority found an unjustified dismissal.
remedies_awarded: $5,355 holiday entitlements; $2,800 notice; $12,242 lost wages; $17,500 compensation.

case_name: ALEX SEEGER v INSTANT FINANCE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [63] Whilst I consider it just to grant leave to Mr Seeger to raise his grievance outside the statutory 90-day time limit, this is not to be taken as an indication of the merits of his substantive claims ... [64] the parties [are directed] to use mediation.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a preliminary leave/out-of-time determination. The Authority expressly disclaimed any view on dismissal merits.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal-merits remedy; leave granted and mediation directed.

case_name: YUANXIANG YANG First v WENJUAN YANG Second Applicant AND KIPPERS EAST LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [68] I am unable to be satisfied on the evidence before me that Mr and Mrs Yang’s resignation was at the instigation of the employer ... [the evidence] does not support a claim of constructive dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review separates the failed constructive-dismissal claims from successful underpayment/disadvantage claims. The applicants resigned to pursue other opportunities and did not establish employer-instigated resignation.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; each applicant received $10,000 disadvantage compensation plus wage/holiday arrears and penalties.

case_name: FIRE AND EMERGENCY NEW ZEALAND v YQL
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [42] FENZ’s removal application does not succeed. The substantive matter between the parties should be determined by the Authority in the first instance and is not to be removed to the Employment Court.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this determination decides only FENZ's application to remove the substantive matter to the Employment Court. The underlying case is an unjustified-disadvantage matter and remains for substantive determination.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal-merits remedy; removal application declined.

case_name: XDC v ALLIED INVESTMENTS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The conduct in issue does not reach the level where it can be said Allied was in breach of the duty of good faith or fair dealing. XDC was not constructively dismissed.
review_notes: Direct review of the resignation, alleged bullying, employer investigations and constructive-dismissal test. Allied's managerial actions and investigations were within the range open to a fair and reasonable employer and did not cause a constructive dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; constructive-dismissal claim failed.

case_name: KEVIN ANDERSON v NEW ZEALAND TRANSPORT AGENCY WAKA KOTAHI
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [52] Mr Anderson’s claim that he was unjustifiably disadvantaged relates to a failure to offer a role on substantially the same terms and conditions and then to pay redundancy compensation. [64] He has not established a personal grievance.
review_notes: Direct review confirms the pleaded claim is unjustified disadvantage concerning redeployment terms/redundancy compensation, not a dismissal-merits grievance.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; disadvantage claim failed.

case_name: CALEB KIRIONA v TE PUKENGA – NZ INSTITUTE OF SKILLS AND TECHNOLOGY
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [40] Mr Kiriona has not made out his claims of unjustified disadvantage, unjustified dismissal and breaches of contract. His claims fail.
review_notes: Direct review of the fixed-term agreement and genuine redundancy. Mr Kiriona accepted the redundancy itself was genuine; the agreement permitted early termination on notice and did not require payment to the fixed-term end date.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; claims failed.

case_name: KAREN CLUNE v ARTHUR D. RILEY AND COMPANY LTD
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The process followed was fair to Ms Clune. She has not established that Arthur D. Riley and Company Ltd failed to act as a fair and reasonable employer could have done in making a decision to dismiss her. Ms Clune’s personal grievance application is declined.
review_notes: Direct second review of the serious-misconduct allegation and dismissal. The Authority found deliberate disobedience of a clear meter-reading instruction after a prior warning and a fair process; it did not separately label the proved conduct serious misconduct in its final finding.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; personal grievance declined.

case_name: MICHAEL REDDY v HAMILTON CITY COUNCIL
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [156] HCC’s final decision to dismiss ... was a decision open to a fair and reasonable employer in all the circumstances at the relevant time. [158] I determine that Mr Reddy was not unjustifiably dismissed by HCC.
review_notes: Direct second review of the misconduct/serious-misconduct process and dismissal. HCC provided extensive support, investigated repeated concerns, gave opportunities to respond and reached a dismissal outcome within the fair-and-reasonable range.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; disadvantage claim also failed.

case_name: MARY BASTION v CASHMERE PRIMARY TE PAE KERERU SCHOOL BOARD
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [35] Ms Bastion did not raise a personal grievance for unjustified dismissal. [37] I do not have jurisdiction to investigate and determine an employment relationship problem based on Ms Bastion’s dismissal. [45] The employment relationship problem ... is struck out.
review_notes: Direct review confirms the Authority disposed of the termination-related claims on grievance/timing and jurisdiction grounds. It did not decide whether the vaccination-order dismissal was justified.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal-merits remedy; proceeding struck out for lack of jurisdiction.

case_name: SHARMAN MATENGA v QSL (NZ) PTY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [1] This determination deals with an application Mr Matenga brings to join FedEx as a controlling third party to personal grievances he has raised with QSL for unjustified constructive dismissal and unjustified disadvantage. [41] Mr Matenga’s application to join FedEx ... is successful.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this determination decides only the controlling-third-party joinder application. It finds an arguable contribution by FedEx but does not decide the underlying constructive-dismissal merits.
remedies_awarded: FedEx joined as controlling third party; substantive dismissal merits remain pending.

case_name: JOSHUA FRENCH v COMMISSIONER OF POLICE
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [1] Constable French ... remains employed. [2] He claims that he has been unjustifiably disadvantaged in his employment by various actions taken by Police.
review_notes: Direct review confirms this is a continuing-employment unjustified-disadvantage/good-faith case, not dismissal merits. Some disadvantage claims succeeded and others failed.
remedies_awarded: $5,250 compensation after 25% contribution for successful disadvantage grievances; no dismissal remedy.

case_name: YIPING CHEN v ARMSTRONG PRESTIGE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [87] I do not find Ms Chen has shown she was constructively dismissed. [88] Yiping Chen’s personal grievance that she was constructively unjustifiably dismissed by Armstrong Prestige Limited is not successful.
review_notes: Direct review of the commission arrangements, reasons for resignation and constructive-dismissal causation. The Authority found no employer breach causing the resignation and rejected all claims.
remedies_awarded: No remedies; constructive-dismissal and commission claims unsuccessful.
